YOUR DIRECTION, NOT A DEADLINE

Seven months. One day at a time.

Build a routine you can keep after the seven months are over.

YOUR INITIAL TARGET · REVIEW AS YOU GO

10 kg toward a lighter, stronger you.

Build a stronger core and follow waist changes without a deadline for visible abs. Reassess your next weight target after this initial goal.

Start with the 10-minute session. This is a starting habit, not the whole weight-loss plan. Gradually add walking and everyday movement. Aim toward at least 150 minutes of moderate activity per week and strength work on at least two days.

NHS activity guidance ↗

01MONTH 1 · FIND YOUR FEET

Build consistency.

Do Foundation 2–3 times a week on nonconsecutive days. Add a comfortable 5–10 minute walk on other days.

  • Learn each movement first.
  • Keep an effort where you can talk.
  • Use extra rest when needed.
10-minute sessions
02MONTHS 2–3 · BUILD YOUR BASE

A little more, gradually.

Keep 2–3 strength days. Try Core & control when you can move comfortably and recover well. Gradually lengthen your walks.

  • Add 5 minutes when a walk feels easy.
  • Work toward 150 activity minutes/week.
  • Leave a recovery day between strength sessions.
10–12-minute sessions
03MONTHS 4–5 · GET STRONGER

Progress with purpose.

Try the 16-minute session if ready. Make one change at a time: more control, a little more range, or a harder variation.

  • Keep the last repetitions controlled.
  • Maintain regular brisk walking.
  • Return to an easier session when needed.
12–16-minute sessions
04MONTHS 6–7 · MAKE IT YOURS

Keep what works.

Maintain your strength habit and activity. Review weight trends, energy and waist changes, rather than chasing a final weigh-in.

  • Review the first 5–10 kg lost before setting another target.
  • Seek coaching if progress stalls.
  • Keep going beyond the target date.
Consistency, then progression
A WEEK YOU CAN REPEAT

Movement. Strength. Recovery.

Fuel the habit.

Include protein, vegetables, fruit and fibre-rich foods. Choose water often, keep portions in view, and use a modest, sustainable energy deficit. Avoid crash diets.

Recovery counts.

Protect a regular sleep routine and leave time for muscles to recover. More soreness is not a better workout. Consistency matters more than exhausting yourself.

Build a stronger core.

Core exercises strengthen your abdomen. They do not selectively burn belly fat. Track strength and optional waist measurements alongside weight. Visible abs have no fixed deadline.

Guidance, sources & important context +

This is a general fitness tool, not an individualized medical or nutrition prescription. Review your starting weight, initial target and plan with a clinician or registered dietitian, especially if you have a health condition, injury or take medication.

Stop exercising and get urgent help for chest pain, fainting or severe/unusual breathlessness.
